members.working:
Heating NaNO3 at ~500°C decomposes to NaNO2 (or Na2NO2?). Typically NaNO3 → NaNO2 + O2 at ~650°C? But approximate 500°C may give NaNO2. Compound

likely NaNO2. Reaction of

with NH4Cl upon boiling yields NH4NO2? Actually NaNO2 + NH4Cl → NH4NO2 + NaCl? But known reaction: NaNO2 + NH4Cl → NH4NO2 + NaCl. NH4NO2 upon heating decomposes to N2O + H2O. However boiling with NH4Cl may give ammonium nitrite which is unstable. Compound likely NH4NO2 (ammonium nitrite). NH4NO2 is paramagnetic? It contains unpaired electrons? NO2- is isoelectronic with O2, which is paramagnetic. NH4NO2 contains NO2- radical? Actually NO2- has 17 electrons, odd? NO2- has 17 electrons, one unpaired? NO2- is isoelectronic with O2 (16) plus one extra electron gives one unpaired? O2 has two unpaired. NO2- has one unpaired? Likely paramagnetic. Bond order of NO2- is 1.5? But maybe N2O? Reaction of with H2 in presence of Fe catalyst at 200 atm and 400-450°C yields a compound . This resembles Haber-like reduction of nitrite to ammonia? Fe catalyst reduces NO to N2? Might produce NH3? Compound likely NH3? Shape trigonal pyramidal? NH3 is trigonal pyramidal. N sp3 hybridised. So options: (A) bond order 2.5? NO2+? Not likely. (B) paramagnetic true for NH4NO2? (C) shape trigonal pyramidal maybe NH3 true. (D) N sp3 true. But only one correct? Probably D only? Choose D.

members.working: NaNO₃ heated ~500°C decomposes to NaNO₂ (P). NaNO₂ + NH₄Cl on boiling gives N₂ (Q) (NaCl + H₂O also formed). N₂ has bond order 3 and is diamagnetic, so (A) and (B) are false. N₂ + 3H₂ over Fe catalyst at 200 atm, 400–450°C is the Haber process giving NH₃ (R). NH₃ is trigonal pyramidal with sp³-hybridised N, so (C) and (D) are correct.
